notes: WebSearch could not be used for this part (the session's search budget was already spent), so pages were reached directly: the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State, government, party and newspaper sites, the papers' own search pages where they answer programs (hometownsource.com and presspubs.com), KAXE's 2026 election guide, and Wikipedia's article pages. Everything was read with the kit's own User-Agent, one request at a time, after each site's robots.txt. Candidates with nothing below (Greg Forcier, Sunny D. Resnick, Tony Preciado, Ali Verney, Melissa Danielson, Myron Matthew Grage, Alan R. Fitterer) are ones for whom no such page stated anything a card may show.

Three campaign websites that were not filed with the Secretary of State were found by asking whether likely addresses exist (an address lookup, not a request to a site) and then reading the ones that did: mallieforjudge.com, votedahlquist.com and reiter4mayor.com. Each names the candidate and the race, as its 'how' line says. Addresses that exist but are not the candidate's, or say nothing: tonypreciado.com (the portfolio of a film effects artist of the same name, not the Mounds View candidate); votepreciado.com (its robots.txt asks programs to stay out, so it was not opened, and nothing ties it to this race); krachmer.com (a page saying the site is under renovation, naming nobody); votedanielson.com, batesforjudge.com, judgechristopherbates.com, keepjudgebates.com and christopherbatesforjudge.com (parking or 'launching soon' pages).

Sites that asked programs to stay out or refused them, so nothing was taken from them and nothing was worked around: brianformn.com (its robots.txt request was answered 403); co.ym.mn.gov and ci.hugo.mn.us (robots.txt shuts out every program it does not name, so there is no county page for John Berends and no city page for Becky Petryk); mncourts.gov (403: no court page for Judge Bates or Judge Mallie); bioguide.congress.gov (robots.txt); the search of southernminn.com (404). Pine Knot News's search page was not tried (another part found it closed); its elections section and stories were read. The endorsement sweep's ledger says Forward Independence's candidates page lists Mike Krachmer for Mayor of Vadnais Heights; that site's robots.txt asks programs to stay out, so this part did not open it and records nothing from it. wrenshall.k12.mn.us did not answer; the district's pages are at isd100.org.

Read and left out on purpose: ages given as 'age on Election Day' (KAXE's guides, for Mary Carlson and Matthew Mallie), which do not fix a birth year; jobs, including school maintenance, sheriff's office ranks, city prosecutor and assistant county attorney posts, an agency's counsel and fire department service; schools; neighborhood, league and association boards; party posts (a county party chair appears only as the candidate's own words); labor and other non-party endorsements; relatives' offices; a 2020 run for a nonpartisan council seat (Joe Reiter); and everything the Legislative Reference Library and the Congressional Directory print about a member's private life.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape other parts use): the Senate District 46 DFL and the Senate District 50 DFL each list Alicia Gibson, for the Edina City Council, under 'Letter of Support', a heading that is not the word endorsement. They are kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision.

For the second reader: (1) Kim Rich: the Senate District 46 Republicans' home page prints his line as 'House District 45B: Kim Rich' under 'SD 46 Endorsed Republican Candidates'. It is taken as the unit's endorsement for House District 46B because the unit is Senate District 46, the two lines above it are Senate District 46 and House District 46A, and the name links to kimrichformn.org, whose home page is headed 'House District 46B'. (2) Amy Klobuchar: the years as Hennepin County Attorney (1999 to 2007) are Wikipedia's; the official Congressional Directory gives only the elections (1998 and 2002). Her birth date and her 2006 election are from the Congressional Directory for the 117th Congress on GovInfo; her Senate service from January 3, 2007 is on the Senate's own list of Minnesota senators. (3) Jimmy Gordon is a sitting member whose roster record has no birth date, so the Legislative Reference Library's is given, as other parts did; the Library lists his time as mayor with dates unknown, and his own site says he joined the Isanti City Council in 2019 and was elected mayor in 2022. (4) Mary Carlson: the district's board page is titled 'Wrenshall School District' and its footer reads 'Carlton-Wrenshall Public School District'; her site says Wrenshall School Board, and in KAXE's guide she says Carlton-Wrenshall School Board. (5) John Berends: the one readable government page naming him is the Board of Health page of Countryside Public Health, the five-county community health board; it does not give his district. (6) Randy (RJ) Heidmann's start year 2023 rests on two statements on the district's page (four-year terms begin the January after the election; his ends in 2026) and on his own answer in KAXE's guide that he was elected in 2022. (7) Todd Madson's start year is the Laker Pioneer's report of the January 9, 2023 swearing-in. (8) Christopher D. Bates: the tie between the 2026 candidate and the 2024 appointee is the name, Minnesota and the First Judicial District; the day he took the bench was not found, so no start year is given. (9) Ryan Shea: ryansheaforsheriff.com is his campaign site from 2022, still up (it asks for a vote 'on November 8th' and calls him Detective Shea); it is not recorded as a website for the 2026 race. (10) Mike Belz's own_words is a statement about party politics on the school board rather than about a party of his own; parts 18 and 21 recorded comparable lines for two others in his race. (11) Tony Compo's township post is as the Pine Knot News described him on May 29, 2026; the township's own site could not be found. (12) Matthew R. Mallie's site is dated by its page data (published September 1, 2026; changed September 28, 2026) and Julian Dahlquist's by the site-builder's own stamp in the page (June 2026). (13) Becky Petryk's 'now' rests on The Citizen's story of September 29, 2026, which quotes her as a council member: https://www.presspubs.com/citizen/newsletter/residents-submit-petition-against-hardwood-creek-trail-extension-project/article_332a798e-2927-4397-b054-9b8d9844929f.html
